question: A charity's donation-thank-you process works well overall but is slow only at the drafting step. Which integration approach is most appropriate?
options: A) Augment the process by having Claude draft, with the same person signing off
B) Redesign the process so donors receive whatever Claude drafts straight away
C) Keep the process as it is and offer Claude as a tool people may use or ignore
D) Redesign the process around Claude and drop the sign-off step that slows it
correct_answers: A) Augment the process by having Claude draft, with the same person signing off
explanations: Correct. When one step is the constraint and the rest of the process is sound, augment that step and leave the controls in place. The sign-off is not what was slow.
Sending unreviewed drafts to donors is an outward-facing, effectively irreversible step and should not be delegated unchecked.
Optional, unstructured use leaves the bottleneck exactly where it was and produces inconsistent letters to donors.
Removing the sign-off removes the check that makes the process safe, in exchange for time that was not being lost there.
